# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 13 (Bu-Vb Ss13)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Ss13
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 13
**Title (English, from literature):** Being a corrupter of families
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuladūsaka* (“Being a corrupter of families”) is the thirteenth rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* section in the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The text concerns a monastic who corrupts lay families, causing local householders to lose faith in the Buddha's teachings. According to the origin narrative, the rule was instituted following the corrupt conduct of the group of six monks (*chabbaggiya*), a faction responsible for offenses prompting many Vinaya rules. Monks guilty of corrupting families are subject to formal banishment from the locality; persistent resistance to banishment after repeated formal admonitions incurs a *saṅghādisesa* offense, entailing suspension. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
